rationale: The proposed topology improves the binding constraints—primarily NF and S21—by introducing a source-degenerated common-source stage with an inductor in the source path to enhance input impedance matching and noise performance, while preserving the low-power and stability characteristics. The addition of the inductor in series with the source of M1 creates a resonant network at 3.5 GHz that improves input match (S11) and simultaneously reduces noise figure by increasing the effective source resistance seen by the gate, which is optimal for low-noise operation in narrowband LNAs. The current mirror (M2–M4) maintains bias current efficiency and gain, while the output load (RL) and output capacitance (Cout) are retained to ensure output matching and gain. This topology is well-suited for H-tier 3.5 GHz LNAs requiring low NF, tight match, and low power.
